security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU TCG/KVM, when ext_zicfilp is enabled but ext_smepmp, ext_zkr, and ext_smmpm are all disabled, the have_mseccfg() CSR predicate at target/riscv/csr.c:779 returns RISCV_EXCP_ILLEGAL_INST, making mseccfg inaccessible despite zicfilp adding the MSECCFG_MLPE field. Conversely, if a future extension adds an mseccfg field but have_mseccfg() is not updated, the CSR will be incorrectly invisible to the guest.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: have_mseccfg\b.*ext_smepmp.*ext_zkr.*ext_smmpm(?!.*ext_\w+).*RISCV_EXCP_ILLEGAL_INST — incomplete extension-to-field mapping where CSR existence check does not enumerate all extensions that contribute fields to mseccfg
security_spec.summary: mseccfg CSR existence predicate (have_mseccfg) incomplete: doesn't check ext_zicfilp (MSECCFG_MLPE field), violating spec rule that mseccfg exists if any extension adds a field to it

findings.finding: have_mseccfg() gates mseccfg CSR visibility on ext_smepmp, ext_zkr, and ext_smmpm, but does NOT check ext_zicfilp. The Zicfilp extension adds the MLPE field (bit 10) to mseccfg per the privileged spec (machine.adoc:2338). When ext_zicfilp is enabled but smepmp/zkr/smmpm are all disabled, mseccfg is incorrectly invisible to the guest (RISCV_EXCP_ILLEGAL_INST), making the MLPE field inaccessible despite being architecturally required. Conversely, if a future extension adds mseccfg fields but have_mseccfg() is not updated, the same pattern will recur.

spec_citations.excerpt: The Zicfilp extension adds the `MLPE` field in `mseccfg`. When `MLPE` field is 1, Zicfilp extension is enabled in M-mode.

==== Machine Security Configuration (`mseccfg`) Register

`mseccfg` is an optional 64-bit read/write register, formatted as shown in <<mseccfg>>, that controls security features.
`mseccfg` exists if `Zkr` is implemented, or if it is required by other processor features.

findings.finding: The ext_zicfilp handling in mseccfg_csr_write() applies a self-OR no-op: val |= (val & MSECCFG_MLPE). This statement has no semantic effect since it ORs val with a value already contained in val. If the intent was to unconditionally set MLPE (sticky bit), it should be `val |= MSECCFG_MLPE`. If the intent was to make MLPE WARL=0 (always 0), it should clear it. As written, it does nothing, which may be correct passive behavior for a regular read/write field (MLPE is not sticky), but the dead-code pattern is suspicious and may mask a copy-paste error from the smepmp sticky-bit logic above.
